name: Field Doctor-Style Chickpea Masala Curry (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
1 x 400 g tin Plum Tomato
435 g Whole grain rice
215 g Potato
215 g Chickpeas
215 g Tofu [Water, SOY beans, Firming Agent: Calcium Sulphate]
1 medium Sweet Potato
1 Green Pepper
3/4 medium Courgettes
120 g Red Quinoa
1 1/2 tbsp Coconut Milk [Coconut, Water]
1 1/2 tbsp Tomato Puree [tomato]
3 tbsp Tapioca Starch
2 1/2 tbsp Turmeric Blend
1/2 Lemon Juice
5 tbsp Coriander
1 1/4 tbsp Ginger
2 tsp Sea Salt
3/4 tbsp Black Onion (Nigella) Seeds
1 1/2 tsp Cumin seeds (whole)
3/4 tsp Garam Masala
2/3 tsp Sweet Noble Paprika
1/3 tsp Brown Sugar
1/2 tsp Curry Leaves
1/2 tsp Chilli Powder
directions:
1. Grains: Cook wholegrain rice and red quinoa; drain and keep warm.

2. Temper spices: Warm extra virgin olive oil with cumin seeds, nigella seeds, curry leaves, ginger, turmeric, garam masala, paprika and chilli powder.

3. Curry: Add chopped tomato, tomato puree, coconut milk, lemon juice, brown sugar and water. Simmer. Stir in chickpeas, cubed tofu, potato, sweet potato, green pepper and courgette. Cook until vegetables are soft and sauce coats them; thicken with tapioca slurry if needed. Season with salt.

4. Finish with coriander. Serve over rice–quinoa.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Chickpea Masala Curry (Low FODMAP) (~391 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/chickpea-masala-curry-low-fodmap
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~391 g x 8 = 3128 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~777 g (inferred ~24.84% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~25 g (inferred ~0.80% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
